question: How do Goldfinch and the other uncollateralized on-chain credit protocols structure risk, and what do first-party and dashboard reads show about their scale on 2026-10-08?

frame.population: on-chain uncollateralized or institutional credit protocols
frame.comparator: Tidepool member credit lines with pooled risk

findings.finding: TranchedPool: each borrower pool has slices, each slice a junior tranche (backers, first loss) and a senior tranche (odd ids); juniorFeePercent (at most 100) is the junior share of senior interest. SeniorPool.invest(pool) deposits into the senior tranche of the latest slice by a strategy; FixedLeverageRatioStrategy returns a leverage ratio from the config, so senior capital is a fixed multiple of junior capital.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: function invest(ITranchedPool pool) external override whenNotPaused nonReentrant returns (uint256)

findings.finding: Losses: SeniorPool.writedown(tokenId) assesses the pool, calculates a writedown percent and amount from lateness and distributes the delta as losses to the senior pool's share price; writedowns reverse if the borrower repays.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: function writedown(uint256 tokenId) external override whenNotPaused nonReentrant

findings.finding: Withdrawals from the senior pool are by epoch since protocol v3.0.0 (2022-11-30): requestWithdrawal, cancelWithdrawalRequest, claimWithdrawalRequest, with usdcAllocated per epoch; there is no instant exit.

Borrower and lender gating: contracts include Go.sol and UniqueIdentity.sol (non-transferable identity tokens) and IRequiresUID on pools. Latest commit in the clone 2025-11-30; packages include goldfinch-prime and protocol-l2.

The docs page states Goldfinch Prime as the current product: "Goldfinch Prime represents the next evolution in that mission", giving individuals access to large private credit managers (named Ares, Apollo, Golub) through one diversified investment, using USDC on Base.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Goldfinch Prime represents the next evolution in that mission

notFound: tranche, underwriting, KYC and default text; the page read does not mention them
total loans originated and total losses

findings.finding: Maple states that yield comes "primarily" from fixed-rate, overcollateralized loans to institutional borrowers, short duration, supported by DeFi liquidity provision and futures basis trading; Syrup makes the institutional lending marketplace available through DeFi. The page mentions only overcollateralized loans.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: fixed rate, overcollateralized loans to institutional borrowers

notFound: undercollateralized lending, pool delegates, defaults and losses; not on the page read
TVL or AUM; the page links to external dashboards

item.title: DeFiLlama reads: peak versus 2026-10-08 TVL for uncollateralized and mutual-risk protocols
